# Results — Study 117 (Pi-Cycle-Top) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Pi-Cycle-Top
indicator — firing when MA(111) crosses above 2×MA(350) on BTC-USD daily closes —
measured against a **random-date control** (2,000 Monte Carlo draws of random starting
days from the same tape). As-of **2026-06-13**; Yahoo daily BTC history starts
2014-09-17, so the 2013 cycle top is outside the observable range.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker  | Window                       | Fingerprint    |
|---------|------------------------------|----------------|
| BTC-USD | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-13      | `7e2bfe41c4d3` |

Indicator parameters: fast=111 days, slow=350 days, multiplier=2.0.  
Warmup required: 350 bars (first usable signal no earlier than late 2015).  
**Signals found on Yahoo tape: 2** (2017-12-16, 2021-04-11).  
Note: the 2024 BTC cycle never triggered the indicator (MA111/2×MA350 peaked at 0.74 in June 2024 — never crossed 1.0).

## Multiplier sensitivity

The "2×" in the indicator is presented as π-encoded (111/350 ≈ π/10). In reality it is
a tunable parameter. Changing it modestly changes the signal count dramatically:

| Multiplier | n signals | Signal dates |
|:----------:|:---------:|:-------------|
| 1.7        | 2         | 2017-07-26, 2021-02-06 |
| 1.8        | 3         | 2017-08-19, 2017-10-20, 2021-02-18 |
| 1.9        | 2         | 2017-11-26, 2021-03-10 |
| 2.0        | 2         | 2017-12-16, 2021-04-11 |
| 2.1        | 1         | 2018-01-08 |
| 2.2        | 0         | — |
| 2.3        | 0         | — |

The multiplier 2.0 was selected because it best aligned with known tops in sample. At
1.8 an extra false positive appears; at 2.1 only one signal fires; at 2.2+ none. This
is the definition of curve-fitting.

## Verdict

### The "call" is visually impressive, statistically empty

The two signals did precede massive drawdowns (−57% and −44% in 90 days). The p-values
look small (0.000 at 90d). But:

1. **n=2 on a 56%-annual-vol asset.** With two events, any cherry-picked negative pair
   of 90-day BTC windows will produce a tiny p-value against a random-day baseline.
   The pi-numerology added nothing — two random crashes in a 4,288-day tape.

2. **The indicator never fired in 2024.** BTC rallied from ~$30,000 to ~$108,000 in
   2024-25. The MA111/2×MA350 ratio peaked at 0.74 in June 2024 — it never crossed the
   threshold. So the indicator *missed the most important cycle* in the out-of-sample period.

3. **Multiplier sensitivity kills the claim.** At mult=2.2 there are zero signals ever.
   At mult=1.8 there are three signals (including a false one in October 2017, which
   *preceded a +300% rally*, not a top). The "π" is a post-hoc rationalization of a
   hand-fitted parameter.

4. **HAC t-stat of −10.9 at n=2 is meaningless.** The high t-stat is a mathematical
   artefact of fitting two consistent data points with a standard error based on n=2.
   It carries no inferential weight.

### Signal — NONE

The effect cannot clear the inference bar: n=2 events, massive asset volatility, and
one missed cycle in the most recent data.

### Tradability — MIRAGE

Even if the signal were real, it fires at most once every 3-4 years, missed the 2024
cycle entirely, and the reverse-engineering from 2-3 tops offers no out-of-sample
credibility. Trading a 3-year-horizon signal on n=2 is not an investment strategy.

### Busted: a curve-fit to 2 tops

The π numerology is decorative. The multiplier 2.0 was selected to hit two known tops.
The 2024 cycle contradicts the pattern. The indicator is a compelling-looking chart story
built on two data points and a mathematical coincidence.
